title: Cosmology: Robertson–Walker spacetimes and the Friedmann equations
summary: Maximally symmetric spaces; the Robertson–Walker metric with k = −1, 0, +1; the Friedmann equations, critical density and equations of state; redshift via a Killing tensor; cosmological distances; the flatness and horizon problems and inflation.

objectives.description: Objectives will be finalised when the unit is prepared; the source material is 8.962 Lectures 18–19 (Lecture Guide pages 5–8) and Carroll Chapter 8.

preparation.description: Read the Lecture Guide's synopsis of Lecture 18 (PDF page 5): maximally symmetric spaces, the Robertson–Walker metric and comoving coordinates.
Read the continuation of Lecture 18 (PDF page 6): k = −1, 0, +1, the scale factor a(t), the Friedmann equations, Ω and the critical density, equations of state.
Read the Lecture Guide's synopsis of Lecture 19 (PDF pages 7–8): redshift via a Killing tensor, distance measures, the flatness and horizon problems, inflation.
Watch Lectures 18 and 19 from the video gallery (transcripts on each lecture page).
Optional: Carroll, Chapter 8 Cosmology (reference-only; 1997 observational statements are historical).
